correctness.rationale: Achievability is obtained by explicit one-sided Gaussian filters. For every successful terminal branch, after branch-dependent Gaussian corrections, exact conversion fixes separately the \( |00\rangle \) and \( |11\rangle \) amplitudes. Summing those identities and applying terminal completeness gives \(P\cos^2\phi\le\cos^2\theta\) and \(P\sin^2\phi\le\sin^2\theta\), yielding the matching upper bound. Boundary cases \(\theta=\phi\) and \(\phi=\pi/4\) agree with identity conversion and the published Bell-distillation construction. The only nonstandard premise, Gaussianity of the filter family, was checked in the 2026 primary source; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result gives the complete exact one-copy stochastic conversion frontier for the canonical two-mode entangled fermionic Gaussian family in the fine-grained GSLOCC model. It turns the older qualitative absence of nontrivial deterministic Gaussian LOCC into a sharp quantitative dilution law, while showing that concentration loses no probability relative to unrestricted LOCC. It also proves optimality of the 2026 Bell-distillation success probability rather than merely reproducing it. These are natural resource-conversion questions attached directly to a fresh literature endpoint, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
